[IAOT.3.1] The `dsc compile` command emits the base `.dsc` — schema /
rule atoms plus the C Rete network (`AlphaNode` / `BetaNode` / `TerminalNode`), which is the
program ([RDSC.4a]). Two flags govern what else the artefact carries,
and what it stops carrying.

`--emit-aot=<arch>` emits `CompiledCode` atoms for `<arch>` and is repeatable.
Given alone it **suppresses** the Rete network. `--emit-rete` keeps the
network alongside the `CompiledCode` atoms, so the artefact still runs where the
compiled code does not; it is a no-op without `--emit-aot`. The shape of
both flags is the `compile_option` production at
`compiler/dsc_cli.ebnf`; what they do to the artefact
is stated here, because a grammar cannot carry it ([STYL.2.15.4]).

**`--emit-aot` is not purely additive**, which is why `--emit-rete`
exists: an AOT-only artefact is the smaller thing an embedded target
wants, and an artefact carrying both is the portable thing a fleet
wants. Neither is a safe default for the other.
